I'm questioning whether the admin logon at 10:01 actually caused the svc-a process to run a minute later just because they're close in time and on the same host—that temporal and spatial proximity alone doesn't establish causation, especially since the process ran under a separate service account rather than the admin's own identity.

A process launched manually by an admin would typically inherit their own context, not run as svc-a, which points more toward a scheduled task or automated service rather than something the admin triggered directly. Without additional evidence like parent process details or a linked logon session, I can't honestly conclude the logon caused the process execution—it's correlation at best.

content.text: Based on this alone you can't attribute causation—the one-minute gap is only correlation, and a process running under the service account svc-a is actually more consistent with a scheduled task or service start than with the interactive admin logon (which would typically spawn processes under the admin's own context), so you'd need linking evidence like process-parent lineage or a shared logon session ID before blaming the 192.0.2.7 logon.
